Title: Covariance-Aware Demapping on Fourier-Curve Constellations

Covariance-Aware Demapping on
Fourier-Curve Constellations
Bin Han∗, Muxia Sun†, H. Vincent Poor‡, and Hans D. Schotten∗§

Abstract—Injecting artificial noise (AN) along the tangent
space of a curved constellation makes each transmitted symbol
induce a Gaussian observation with a symbol-dependent rank-
one covariance, so the matched maximum-likelihood (ML)
decoder differs from the Euclidean nearest-neighbor decoder
by a single rank-one correction per candidate. We develop
a baseband-demapper realization of this correction for the
Fourier-curve constellation and instantiate a regular (3, 6) low-
density parity-check (LDPC)-coded link at (k, M)=(20, 64).
Against four baselines (Euclidean-mismatched, flat-constellation
isotropic-AN,

erating range by approximately 5 dB over the Euclidean-
mismatched counterpart on the same tangent-AN transmitter,
at a cost of 2kM additional multiply-accumulate operations
per symbol (+50%/+100% under residual/template-correlation
accounting) and a 20 KB constellation–tangent lookup table
(10 KB incremental over a Euclidean template-only LUT). A
bit-interleaved coded-modulation achievable-rate (BICM-AIR)
computation supports the same matched-metric advantage at
the tested labeling and max-log demapper, indicating that the
BLER gain is not merely an artifact of this particular LDPC
simulation, and a Woodbury extension generalizes the rank-one
correction to per-tone Ricean fading. In the tested Monte-Carlo
runs, a design-aware bounded-search eavesdropper without the
phase-key shows no successful LDPC decoding at any tested
k ∈{2, 8, 20} within a B=103 non-code-aided search budget;
code-aided, multi-frame, and known-preamble attacks are left
to follow-up work. LUT quantization down to 6 bits yields no
measurable coded-BLER degradation at the tested operating
points.1
Index Terms—Artificial noise, Fourier-curve constellation,
covariance-aware decoding, soft demapping, LDPC.
I. INTRODUCTION
Classical null-space artificial noise (AN) schemes share
a common structural goal: to render the injected noise or-
thogonal to the legitimate receiver while remaining effective
against the eavesdropper, both within the wiretap-channel
framework of Wyner [2] and Csisz´ar–K¨orner [3] and through
the multi-antenna constructions of Goel and Negi [4], Khisti
and Wornell [5], and the surveys of Mukherjee et al. [6] and
Niu et al. [7]. The orthogonality in those constructions is built
from the channel: spatial degrees of freedom provide a null
space of the legitimate link into which AN can be placed,
every codeword sees the same projector, and the effective
noise covariance is symmetric across codewords. In many
such designs, after ideal Bob-side nulling or whitening, an
1Exact detection-theoretic analysis is developed in a companion letter [1].
additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN)-type Euclidean met-
ric suffices—a setting that differs from the symbol-dependent
covariance considered here.
This channel-based construction has two practical gaps.
The legitimate null space tracks the instantaneous channel
through channel state information (CSI), and staleness or
estimation error leaks AN power directly into the signal
space [6]. Orthogonality with respect to Bob’s channel also
fails to imply orthogonality with respect to Eve’s whenever
the two links are spatially correlated.
A recent companion letter [1] follows an alternative
route, deriving the legitimate advantage from knowledge
of the signal manifold rather than of the channel. On a
curved constellation, AN injected along the local tangent
space rotates with the transmitted symbol; the per-hypothesis
observation covariance is therefore rank-one and symbol-
dependent—a candidate-dependent covariance label carried
by the modulation. The matched maximum-likelihood (ML)
decoder that exploits this label differs from the Euclidean
nearest-neighbor rule by a single rank-one correction per
candidate, and the resulting gap is exactly a mismatched-
decoding gap [8], [9]. The mechanism is adjacent to di-
rectional modulation [10], [11], but it carries no candidate-
dependent covariance label and creates no spatial-direction
selectivity. The model assumes a post-equalization AWGN
real-equivalent baseband channel in which the k subcarri-
ers/samples are synchronized and equalized; the legitimate
advantage rests on a shared phase-key, and a bounded-search
eavesdropper without that key is evaluated in Sec. IV as a
robustness baseline. Information-theoretic secrecy analysis is
left to follow-up work.
The letter [1] develops the detection theory and leaves open
whether the matched metric is realizable as a lightweight
baseband demapper and whether its gain persists under
standard channel coding. The present paper addresses both
questions. We build the LDPC-coded link end-to-end and
report block-error-rate (BLER) curves with 95% Clopper–
Pearson bands across SNR, AN fraction, and LUT bit-width.
A metric-level BICM achievable-rate (AIR) comparison con-
firms the matched-vs-Euclidean gap at the information-rate
level, and a Woodbury extension of the rank-one correction
recovers reliable matched detection under per-tone Ricean
fading where the static-σc demapper saturates. The added
cost is 2kM MAC operations per symbol (+50%/ + 100%)

C. Eavesdropper model
The matched decoder operates correctly because Bob
knows the deployed tangent frame; an attacker without access
to φ faces a different decoding problem. Eve is co-located
(YE = Y ) and design-aware: she knows (1), M, k, β, σc,
the matched rule (7), the LDPC code, and the max-log LLR
demapping [13]. She does not know φ.

III. LINK ARCHITECTURE
The matched rule fits into a legacy AWGN chain with
only two new blocks (Fig. 2): the tangent-AN injector at
the Tx and the rank-one correction in the soft demapper
at the Rx. Every other block follows a standard DSP role;
synchronization, channel estimation, key distribution, and
fixed-point interfacing are not modeled.
The shared LUT {¯xi, ˆti} is fixed across the evaluated
block: the transmitter reads one row per symbol, while the
receiver scans all M rows. The Tx AN branch reads ˆtsℓ
and multiplies it by √β zℓ, zℓ∼N(0, 1), summed into
the transmit signal to realise (4). On the Rx side, two MF
banks indexed by candidate i share the LUT—the Euclidean
bank emits ∥ri∥2/σ2

B. Coded BLER
At β=0.3 the matched decoder reaches BLER=10−1 near
−3.8 dB, ≈5.1 dB earlier than B1 on the same transmitter
(Fig. 3(a)); the gap widens at lower BLER and follows
from the rank-one correction in (7). B2’s isotropic covariance
makes its Euclidean decoder already ML, so Bob’s reliability
matches this flat baseline rather than exceeding it; B3 (no
AN) bounds the BLER cost of diverting signal power into
AN. B4 stays at BLER=1 across the sweep even at 20×
the energy budget, ruling out repetition combining as the
source of the matched gain; richer same-SE coded baselines
are deferred to follow-up work. Across the β-sweep at three
ρslot points (Fig. 3(b)), the matched decoder remains robust
whereas Euclidean degrades sharply near β≈0.25, consistent
with [1].

D. Quantization robustness
The matched decoder’s practicality depends on the LUT’s
robustness to coarse quantization and on the tolerance re-
quired in estimating (σc, β). Across 6–32 bits, no measurable
BLER degradation is observed for either demapper at three
operating points σc ∈{0.20, 0.24, 0.28} spanning the pre-,
mid-, and post-waterfall regions at β=0.3 (Fig. 5); the Tx
and Rx share the same quantized LUT, so quantized tan-
gents enter as a coupled perturbation rather than a receiver-
only mismatch, and the demapper retains the unit-tangent
Sherman–Morrison denominator σ2

VI. CONCLUSION
We have realized matched ML decoding on phase-keyed
Fourier-curve constellations as a rank-one correction added
to a Euclidean nearest-neighbor demapper, costing 2kM
MACs and 10 KB of incremental LUT storage per symbol.
At (k, M)=(20, 64) with regular (3, 6) LDPC coding the
matched decoder extends the BLER=10−1 operating range
by approximately 5 dB over its Euclidean-mismatched coun-
terpart; the BICM achievable rate confirms the same gap,
and a Woodbury extension preserves the rank-one structure
under per-tone Ricean fading. Code-aided, multi-frame, and
known-preamble eavesdropper attacks, information-theoretic
secrecy bounds, and standard-compliant code and labeling
sweeps are left to future work.

Abstract: Injecting artificial noise (AN) along the tangent space of a curved constellation makes each transmitted symbol induce a Gaussian observation with a symbol-dependent rank- one covariance, so the matched maximum-likelihood (ML) decoder differs from the Euclidean nearest-neighbor decoder by a single rank-one correction per candidate. We develop a baseband-demapper realization of this correction for the Fourier-curve constellation and instantiate a regular (3, 6) low- density parity-check (LDPC)-coded link at (k, M)=(20, 64). Against four baselines (Euclidean-mismatched, flat-constellation isotropic-AN, no-AN, and same-spectral-efficiency narrow- band), the matched decoder extends the BLER=10−1 op- erating range by approximately 5 dB over the Euclidean- mismatched counterpart on the same tangent-AN transmitter, at a cost of 2kM additional multiply-accumulate operations per symbol (+50%/+100% under residual/template-correlation accounting) and a 20 KB constellation–tangent lookup table (10 KB incremental over a Euclidean template-only LUT). A bit-interleaved coded-modulation achievable-rate (BICM-AIR) computation supports the same matched-metric advantage at the tested labeling and max-log demapper, indicating that the BLER gain is not merely an artifact of this particular LDPC simulation, and a Woodbury extension generalizes the rank-one correction to per-tone Ricean fading. In the tested Monte-Carlo runs, a design-aware bounded-search eavesdropper without the phase-key shows no successful LDPC decoding at any tested k ∈{2, 8, 20} within a B=103 non-code-aided search budget; code-aided, multi-frame, and known-preamble attacks are left to follow-up work. LUT quantization down to 6 bits yields no measurable coded-BLER degradation at the tested operating points.1
